claim: Non-human animals can pass relational matching tests, but only after heavy training, and perceptual cues keep interfering (baboons 77% correct in re-encoding task; consistent vs inconsistent trials 96.3% vs 62.2%).
agent_test: n/a (animal result); background for O7

claim: Relational match-to-sample is acquired by very few non-human primates: 6 of 29 baboons, no rhesus over 10,000 to 260,000 trials, capuchins only without screens; humans reach 99%.
agent_test: n/a

claim: The gap is graded, not all-or-none: crows, bumblebees (distant-object condition) and chimps with symbols show some relational success, which supports continuity accounts against the strict Penn et al. discontinuity.
agent_test: n/a

claim: Human infants and toddlers show relational generalisation under limits (4 items yes, 5-6 no; same condition 68% vs different at chance), so humans also have a bounded early relational system.
agent_test: n/a

claim: Apes use structured relational similarity less than humans (humans 98% variance by a structural model, apes 58% in Task 1, and featural in Task 2).
agent_test: n/a

claim: Plain GPT-3 matched or beat average humans on digit matrices (generative OR 1.88, multiple choice OR 6.27) and verbal analogies, with a semantic-distance effect (OR 3.24).
agent_test: Run a matched digit-matrix set at equal tokens: plain vs scaffold with O7 analogy operator.

claim: The same GPT-3 result is fragile: on counterfactual alphabets, humans stay at 0.753 while GPT-3 0.488, GPT-3.5 0.350, GPT-4 0.452; GPT-3 generative accuracy fell below 0.1 on a synthetic alphabet.
agent_test: Evaluate scaffold on permuted-alphabet letter strings; compare to plain at equal tokens.

claim: Counterfactual failure is partly a reading problem: comprehension checks are near 1.0 for GPT-4, many errors are valid alternative rules (46% GPT-4; humans 38.59%), and GPT-4 with code execution matches humans (P=0.496). New: models also lack prerequisites (ordered-alphabet rules) and fail to apply an encoded relation (patching fixes up to 38%).
agent_test: Give the agent a code tool for rule checking; measure drop on counterfactual items.

claim: LLM analogy accuracy depends on surface form: reordering pairs drops LLMs (Claude 3 coef -1.78, GPT-4 -1.68, Llama -2.34, all p<0.001) but not humans; GPT-4 and Llama fall on generalised structure while Claude 3 holds.
agent_test: Shuffle example order in few-shot relational prompts; scaffold should be invariant. Test order-averaging.

claim: Models have a deficit on abstract grid reasoning: ConceptARC humans over 90% on 11 of 16 concepts; GPT-4 under 30% on 15 of 16; ARC program best under 80%. Update 2025: reasoning model o3 reaches 77.1% text vs humans 73.0%, so the accuracy gap closes for text, but about 27% of its correct answers use unintended rules.
agent_test: Run ConceptARC subset with and without a rule-induction step at equal tokens.

claim: Text format hurts relational reasoning for LLMs: ACRE GPT-4 0.272 text vs 0.512 symbolic; and vision-language models trail children on KiVA except rotation and colour.
agent_test: Re-encode relational problems symbolically before reasoning (O7 pre-step).

claim: Prompting for analogy helps modestly: self-generated analogical exemplars gave GSM8K GPT-3.5 77.8 vs 75.8 CoT; large gains only for weak models (davinci-003 14.8 to 61.0).
agent_test: Add self-generated analogous problems as a scaffold step; measure at equal tokens versus plain CoT.

claim: Architectures with explicit relational bottlenecks generalise out of distribution where standard nets fail (ESBN+TCN 100.0 vs Transformer 73.7 at m=95, 56.1 at m=98; RMTS 99.7 vs 28.0).
agent_test: Not testable by scaffold; informs what a scaffold must emulate: separating roles from content.

claim: Fine-tuned CLIP learns same/different that transfers to OOD sets (>95% median) and small nets can learn relations from few examples with the right encoding.
agent_test: not directly

claim: Human relational matching is sensitive to load and scaffolds: concurrent load lowers matching (.865 vs .913) and 20% of humans stall at similarity in the 60s, so the perceptual-conceptual barrier exists in humans too.
agent_test: Test whether stalling is reduced by stepwise fading (similarity ladder) in agent prompts.

claim: Wu et al. style counterfactual drops (arithmetic near-perfect to near-zero in some bases; MiniSCAN above 80% to near zero) show reciting rather than abstracting in tasks beyond analogy.
agent_test: Use counterfactual variants as a regression test for any new operator.

claim: Accuracy gap closed, competence gap not: o3 beats humans on ConceptARC text (77.1 vs 73.0) but ~27% of its correct outputs use unintended or wrong rules (humans ~7%); in vision, correct-intended rules exceed correct grids by 7.5-17.7 points.
agent_test: Have the agent state the rule, then test it against an object-level paraphrase and a recoded variant; compare accuracy and rule-intended rate to plain reasoning at equal tokens.

claim: More reasoning tokens do not rescue relational generalisation under range and noise shifts: o3-mini 86.6 to 17.0 on I-RAVEN-X with 3.4x tokens, R1 80.6 to 23.2, while a neuro-symbolic model keeps 88.0.
agent_test: Test a rule-induce-then-execute scaffold on I-RAVEN-X style shifted ranges at matched tokens.

claim: 2026 frontier VLMs choose the relational match on animal-style RMTS (GPT-5.4, Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro 100%); weak models are object-biased (GPT-5.4-mini 32.2, Haiku 4.5 42.5) and CoT lifts them to 83.4 and 99.9. This contradicts the 2024 preprint claim that language models fail RMTS.
agent_test: Run RMTS items with and without a write-the-relation step on a small model.

claim: Penn et al. 2008 argues a symbolic-relational discontinuity across domains, with a chunking/entropy deflation of same-different and RMTS; the key quantitative cases are baboons at chance on 2-icon different trials, 14,576 extra trials for conceptual same/different, and one unreplicated ape (Sarah) for true analogy.
agent_test: n/a

claim: Explicit abstraction before mapping helps far analogies but not near ones in small open models (MCQ 0.45 vs 0.28 Llama; ARN near CoT 0.79 vs 0.69), with no equal-token test on frontier models.
agent_test: Equal-token test: CoT vs extract-roles-then-apply on far-analogy items.
